characters.name: Major Zhao

characters.description: A member of Giraud's stealth boarding team and Bishop's unofficial bodyguard. She approaches one of the infected Keeper dropships through a meteor cloud in sealed combat armor.
characters.name: Ranger Lauren Poole

characters.description: The de facto leader of the captured Keepers and a committed Kristang loyalist. In quarantine, he learns that his team was unknowingly sent to spread a pathogen and that every Keeper carries a delayed kill implant.
characters.name: Colonel Chisolm

characters.description: A British Keeper among the captured infiltration force. Less committed than Chisolm, he reacts to evidence that Earth survived and that his family may still be alive.
characters.name: Lieutenant Nigel Green

recaps.ending:
The Flying Dutchman covertly stops the Paradise attack without exposing itself to the Ruhar fleet. Smythe and Giraud seize both dropships and all twenty infected Keepers. Adams sends the captured Kristang destroyer into the local star, while Skippy disables the captives' programmed kill implants, cures their infection, and develops vaccines for humans and Ruhar. Paradise receives the pathogen analysis and manufacturing instructions, begins large-scale testing, and keeps its human population under quarantine while confidence in the vaccines grows. Chisolm remains a prisoner after resisting the cure trial, while Green and the other Keepers are successfully treated.

Bishop, Skippy, Adams, Chotek, Smythe, Giraud, and the rest of the Dutchman crew set course for Earth. Nagatha's restoration remains incomplete, and Skippy has only begun cautiously sharing advanced science. Perkins, the Mavericks, Nert, Janes, and the Camp Alpha survivors remain alive on Paradise. With X-Force close to dissolution, Perkins wins support from General Lynn to develop an unapproved Ruhar-aligned alien legion, and David Chica postpones civilian plans to stay available. The unresolved strategic threats are the Kristang civil war, Skippy's potential to become a rogue AI, and wormhole emissions likely to reveal humanity's activity to the Thuranin in less than sixty years.
recaps.in_short: An Elder energy virus disables the Flying Dutchman just as the crew learns Paradise faces a bioweapon attack. Meanwhile, Perkins's Mavericks survive the destruction of a Ruhar training cruiser, take command of its cadets, reach Camp Alpha, and recover proof that Kristang forces plan to use human Keepers as carriers for a lethal Ruhar pathogen. After the Mavericks are rescued and Paradise imposes quarantine, Bishop restores the Dutchman, refuels, and enters the system covertly. Smythe and Giraud capture both Keeper dropships, Adams destroys their mission ship, and Skippy disables the captives' kill implants before producing a cure and vaccines. The treatment data reaches Paradise and prevents the immediate catastrophe. The Dutchman heads home, while Perkins remains quarantined and proposes rebuilding X-Force as a Ruhar-aligned alien legion. Earth still faces probable Thuranin detection within sixty years, and evidence that another Elder AI destroyed a civilization leaves Skippy's own long-term safety unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Joe commands the Flying Dutchman with the indispensable assistance of Skippy, an Elder AI whose abilities humanity cannot reproduce. Adams, Smythe, Giraud, Chotek, Chang, Desai, Friedlander, and Simms are among the returning mission personnel, while the communications submind Nagatha is inactive. On Paradise, UNEF officer Emily Perkins leads a small human team working with the Ruhar. Humanity's survival and freedom remain tied to alien powers and technology it does not control.

The Flying Dutchman loses all usable power when Skippy identifies a Guardian tracer from earlier salvage as an energy virus. The contamination migrates between connected power stores and could enter human bodies, so the crew evacuates in fully drained suits. Mechanical starters and hand-cranked generators restore life support outside the ship while Skippy begins a complete purge. He also gives the crew limited ship-control capability and agrees to attempt Nagatha's restoration. Before the crisis is resolved, Joe learns that Paradise faces extinction.

On Paradise, Perkins's six-person team and its young Ruhar liaison, Nert, take part in a war game. Shauna Jarrett, Jesse Coulter, and the other ground soldiers draw off a larger cadet force while Irene and Derek hide a damaged fighter underwater and ambush three aircraft. The exercise validates the humans' unconventional methods. A politically connected senior cadet challenges their conduct, but a Ruhar general rejects the complaint, records their damaged fighter as expendable, and endorses Nert's continued service with the team.

Perkins receives a formal promotion and her unit becomes the Mavericks, a test case for placing human personnel aboard Ruhar ships. After intensive preparation, the team joins a training cruiser staffed largely by cadets. They meet a Ruhar-allied Kristang population distinct from the hostile society they previously knew. Nert faces hostility from the senior cadet, but a human-assisted talent performance improves his standing among his peers.

The cruise becomes dangerous when a Ruhar battle group investigates the wreckage of a civilian vessel. It returns with heavy damage after direct Bosphuraq intervention, suggesting that more advanced patron species are entering the regional fighting themselves. The training cruiser has no combat assignment for the Mavericks, although Nert reports to damage control. A Jeraptha star carrier orders every surviving Ruhar ship to attach under emergency conditions. The cruiser secures last, and the carrier jumps away immediately, leaving the cause of the urgent retreat unknown.

A Bosphuraq battlecruiser attacks the returning force, destroys the training cruiser's bridge, and kills most adult officers. Irene and Derek make an untrained jump from auxiliary control before inbound missiles arrive. Perkins reaches engineering by an exterior spacewalk, and the sole surviving Ruhar officer formally gives her command before dying. A politically connected senior cadet attempts to remove the humans and allied Kristang, but Janes stops the mutiny and supports Perkins. She puts the failed mutineers to work because the badly damaged ship has only days of reactor life.

Perkins returns to the battle site, where the survivors find the aft portion of the Jeraptha carrier Deal Me In and rescue a Jeraptha crewman. The carrier's jump equipment still works, and an onboard emulator can connect it to the Ruhar cruiser's controls. After test jumps and an Elder wormhole transit, the combined wreck reaches the Camp Alpha system on its last stored charge. Its reactor then fails completely. Forced into dropships, Perkins's mixed group detects a small Kristang research force and makes a hidden landing on the planet.

At Camp Alpha, Perkins discovers that Kristang researchers used kidnapped humans in bioweapon work. Their current plan infects unsuspecting human Keepers, who can carry and spread a pathogen lethal to Ruhar. A transport left for Paradise eighteen days earlier. Remote access cannot retrieve the protected research, so Perkins attacks the base before its systems can erase the evidence.

The Mavericks and their allies spoof the base sensors and destroy its main defenses. An improvised missile truck damages Perkins's dropship, but Janes and Jesse destroy the launcher. An allied fighter pilot intercepts the final missile to save Perkins and is presumed dead. The ground force reaches the research compound and Keeper enclosure. David Chica and Jesse prevent loyalists from killing a former acquaintance who wants rescue, while Janes and a Jeraptha analyst recover the memory core and decryption keys. The base activates an atomic self-destruct, but the overloaded survivors escape in a damaged dropship. They have evidence but no pathogen sample. Because they may have been exposed and cannot test themselves during the long incubation period, the entire group hides near its crippled craft and waits.

The Jeraptha merchant ship Sure Thing follows evidence of Deal Me In's survival to Camp Alpha. Its crew initially refuses to bring potentially infected humans aboard, but the former anti-Perkins cadet will not leave without the Mavericks, and the Jeraptha analyst invokes fleet authority. The survivors evacuate in isolated dropships. On Paradise, General Lynn learns that the infection plan may already be underway. With no sample, the Ruhar cannot identify carriers or quickly produce a vaccine. Authorities begin confining humans in southern Lemuria, and military planners consider eliminating the human population the only certain way to remove the threat.

Aboard the still-disabled Flying Dutchman, Joe insists they must intervene once the ship can move. Friedlander's chemical fuel-cell approach lets Joe and Desai restart a Condor without giving the energy virus an active electrical target. The recovery teams retrieve the stranded crew. Joe then proposes ejecting the power-cell bank where Skippy has concentrated the contamination. The plan works, restoring the reactors and propulsion. The ship has lost reserve capacity and needs fuel, but it can finally turn toward Paradise.

Skippy and Bishop determine that the infected Keepers will descend in aeroshells hidden within an approaching meteor shower. During a risky gas-giant refueling stop, Skippy extracts data from the dead Elder AI found on Newark and concludes that an AI with a matrix like his helped move the planet and destroy its intelligent inhabitants. Fearing he could become a similar threat, Skippy asks Bishop to isolate or destroy him. Bishop refuses and argues that Skippy may be humanity's best defense against another rogue AI.

A mechanical failure then cripples Samantha Reed's Condor deep in the gas giant. Bishop connects it by cable to Captain Porter's craft, and the two crews reach orbit in an improvised tow. The Dutchman proceeds with enough fuel for the mission and return. Skippy conceals its arrival at Paradise inside a moon's atmosphere, then locates and infiltrates an obsolete Kristang destroyer. Its data leads to two stealth dropships carrying the infected Keepers. With only sixteen hours before deployment, the crew chooses capture over destruction so Skippy can obtain samples and create countermeasures. Smythe prepares a covert assault on both craft.

Smythe and Giraud lead sealed boarding teams through the meteor cloud while Skippy feeds false images to the dropships' sensors. Both teams kill the Kristang pilots, stun the Keepers, and seize the craft without exposing the Dutchman. Skippy takes full control of the mission destroyer, and Adams sends it into the local star. A buoy left for the Ruhar explains that the attack was stopped and provides an initial pathogen assessment.

The twenty captives learn that they were intended to infect humans and Ruhar on Paradise. They also discover that Kristang implants were set to kill them weeks after landing, and they consent to having the devices disabled. Chisolm remains loyal to the Kristang, while Green responds to proof that Earth and his family survived. Skippy identifies another looming danger: evidence from the repeatedly used Earth wormhole should reach Thuranin sensors in less than sixty years. Humanity cannot yet defend itself independently.

Skippy develops a cure for infected humans and vaccines for both species. Green joins the first volunteer trial, the treatment succeeds, and the remaining captives are treated. Skippy transmits analysis and manufacturing instructions through a Ruhar relay. Paradise begins large-scale human vaccine trials and separate Ruhar testing. With the immediate outbreak prevented, the Flying Dutchman starts home.

The Flying Dutchman has captured both Keeper dropships, destroyed the Kristang mission ship, and delivered a working cure and vaccines to Paradise. The treated Keepers remain prisoners, and Paradise's humans remain quarantined while Ruhar confidence in the countermeasures develops. Bishop and the surviving Dutchman crew head toward Earth with a damaged ship, worn dropships, and enough fuel to return. Skippy is still attempting Nagatha's restoration and cautiously testing limited scientific disclosure. The evidence of a destructive Elder AI and the approaching Thuranin detection deadline remain unresolved.

On Paradise, Emily Perkins and the Mavericks survive but face an uncertain future because UNEF X-Force is close to dissolution. Perkins proposes reorganizing it as a Ruhar-aligned alien legion able to perform ground-security work, gather intelligence, and support longer-term cooperation between species. General Lynn agrees to help develop the proposal, although UNEF leadership and the Ruhar administrator have not approved it. David Chica postpones a possible civilian brewery venture to remain available for the new mission. The book closes with the bioweapon catastrophe averted and Perkins pursuing a new role for the Mavericks.

characters.description: A physically immense, slow-thinking dentist who practices from rooms on Polk Street in San Francisco despite having no formal diploma. He enjoys a narrow routine of work, heavy meals, beer, and music from his concertina. His friend Marcus brings Trina to him for dental treatment, disturbing that settled life.
characters.name: McTeague

characters.description: Marcus Schouler's young cousin, brought to McTeague's rooms because she has broken a tooth. She belongs to a thrifty Swiss-German family and is quiet and conventional when McTeague first meets her.
characters.name: Trina Sieppe

characters.description: McTeague's closest friend and Trina's cousin. Talkative, excitable, and fond of presenting himself as knowledgeable, he works at a dog hospital and initially treats McTeague as a trusted companion.
characters.name: Marcus Schouler

characters.description: The Mexican-born woman who does cleaning in the Polk Street building and searches its refuse for objects she can sell. She repeatedly tells a confused family story about a lost service of gold plate.
characters.name: Maria Macapa

characters.description: An elderly bookbinder who lives in the room beside Miss Baker's. Gentle and intensely shy, he has silently loved his neighbor for years, sharing small routines with her while neither speaks openly about their affection.
characters.name: Old Grannis

characters.description: An older dressmaker who occupies a room adjoining Old Grannis's. She is as reserved as he is and takes comfort in hearing him work through the thin partition, though their mutual attachment remains unspoken.
characters.name: Miss Baker

characters.description: A Jewish junk dealer who buys Maria's finds. His imagination is seized by her tale of vanished gold, and he presses her to repeat every detail whenever she visits his shop.
characters.name: Zerkow

characters.description: Trina's energetic mother and the forceful organizer of the Sieppe household. Practical, noisy, and attentive to propriety, she closely supervises her daughter's courtship and family arrangements.
characters.name: Mrs. Sieppe

characters.description: Trina's father, an immigrant who makes ornamental wooden animals and other carved goods. He is more subdued than his wife and generally follows her lead in family matters.
characters.name: Mr. Sieppe

characters.description: Trina's small younger brother, whose family pronunciation of August sounds like Owgooste. He accompanies the Sieppes at public and family occasions and requires frequent attention from his mother.
characters.name: August Sieppe

characters.description: A harness maker and one of the men in McTeague and Marcus's Polk Street social circle. He joins their evenings of drinking and conversation and serves as a familiar witness to the friendship between them.
characters.name: Mr. Heise

recaps.ending: After killing Trina and taking her savings, McTeague escapes San Francisco. He works at a remote mine until the prospect of arrest drives him farther into the desert. Marcus, now part of the pursuing party, follows him into Death Valley. McTeague has found water and could survive, but Marcus catches him and the former friends fight beside McTeague's exhausted mule. McTeague kills Marcus, only to discover that Marcus has handcuffed their wrists together and thrown away the key. The mule is dead, the water has spilled, and the stolen money lies nearby. The novel closes with McTeague stranded in lethal heat, chained to Marcus's corpse and without a means of escape.
recaps.in_short: McTeague, an unlicensed San Francisco dentist, marries Trina Sieppe after she wins five thousand dollars in a lottery. Trina refuses to spend the principal and develops an obsessive attachment to money, while Marcus Schouler, who yielded Trina to his friend, grows jealous of both the marriage and the prize. Marcus reports McTeague's lack of credentials, destroying his practice. As the couple descend into poverty, McTeague becomes abusive and Trina's hoarding becomes more extreme. He leaves, returns to rob her, and kills her for the savings she has hidden. Pursued after fleeing to mining country, McTeague crosses Death Valley. Marcus catches him there and handcuffs them together during their final struggle. McTeague kills Marcus, but the key is lost, their water is gone, and he is left chained to the body in the desert beside the stolen gold.

recaps.text: McTeague lives alone above Polk Street, where he works as a dentist without formal qualifications and follows a simple daily routine. His friend Marcus Schouler brings his cousin Trina Sieppe to have a damaged tooth treated. McTeague is immediately attracted to her, though he has little experience of courtship or of examining his own feelings. The building's other residents include the shy older neighbors Old Grannis and Miss Baker, each privately attached to the other, and Maria Macapa, who cleans rooms and sells discarded objects. Maria tells the junk dealer Zerkow an uncertain story about gold plate once owned by her family; Zerkow cares less about her than about the treasure he imagines behind the tale.

McTeague's interest in Trina becomes a determined courtship. Marcus, who had hoped to marry his cousin himself, steps aside and takes pride in giving his friend the opportunity. Trina initially resists McTeague's proposal but eventually accepts him. At the same time, a lottery ticket she bought from Maria wins five thousand dollars. The prize transforms the match in Marcus's eyes: what he once regarded as a generous sacrifice begins to look like the loss of a wealthy wife. McTeague and Trina marry and establish their own household. Trina insists that the lottery capital remain invested, allowing them to use only its interest, and her careful management at first appears to promise security.

Marcus's resentment surfaces in increasingly open hostility toward McTeague. Their former companionship breaks down, and a violent quarrel makes clear that Marcus now believes he surrendered both Trina and her fortune. Before leaving San Francisco, he retaliates by informing the authorities that McTeague has no diploma or license. McTeague is ordered to stop practicing dentistry, removing the work on which the household depends. Trina will not draw upon the five-thousand-dollar principal to cushion the loss. The couple begin selling possessions and moving into poorer rooms, while McTeague struggles to replace a trade that had defined his limited but stable life.

Poverty magnifies the traits that had already shaped the marriage. Trina cuts every expense and becomes consumed by the security and physical presence of her savings, even as she earns small sums by carving wooden animals. McTeague, deprived of his practice and comforts, grows coarse and violent. He abuses Trina and pressures her for money, while she accepts worsening conditions rather than touch the lottery principal. Elsewhere, Zerkow's fixation on Maria's supposed lost treasure turns their household into another destructive struggle over imagined wealth. Old Grannis and Miss Baker, by contrast, finally move beyond their long silence and find modest companionship with one another.

McTeague separates from Trina but returns when he needs money. Trina now lives cheaply and hides her savings while taking intense pleasure in handling the coins. McTeague attacks and kills her, then takes the money and flees San Francisco. He travels through California mining country and finds work, briefly returning to the labor of his youth. News that officers are searching for him forces him onward again. Rather than remain near settlement, he heads into increasingly barren country, relying on his great strength and an instinctive awareness that pursuit is closing in behind him.

McTeague enters Death Valley with a mule, limited water, and the money stolen from Trina. Marcus is among the pursuers and follows him into the desert. The former friends confront each other in the extreme heat. During their fight Marcus handcuffs his wrist to McTeague's and throws away the key, ensuring that McTeague cannot simply escape. McTeague kills Marcus, but the victory leaves him trapped: the mule has died, the water container has been destroyed, and no key can free him from the corpse. With Trina's gold still beside him, McTeague is stranded in Death Valley without water or any practical hope of survival.
